title.narrative: Improving food security of households affected by El Nino-induced drought in Manica and Sofala provinces

description.narrative: Mozambique is highly vulnerable to climate shocks which results in frequent droughts, floods, and cyclones. These events disproportionately affect vulnerable households mostly rainfed agricultural communities. Increased drought frequency continues to drive humanitarian crises as communities experience reduced food production, income loss, and limited access to essential services.The 2023 El Niño worsened Mozambique’s food insecurity. Disrupted rainfall and temperature patterns heavily impacted agriculture, with Ministry of Agriculture assessments revealing 19% reduction in crop yields across 591,541 hectares, or a loss of 720,000 tons of cereals. This is in a country where 70% of the population rely on agriculture for substance. Rising food prices further strain households. The lives and livelihoods of people are threatened.In priority districts of Guro, Macossa, Tambara (Manica), and Maringue (Sofala), the drought affected over 189,000 people, including 72,000 classified as IPC Phase 4, who requires urgent assistance. These areas face compounded threats from drought and seasonal flooding due to their location in the Zambeze River basin. Poor harvests have led to displacements and coping strategies including migration to areas with better agricultural conditions and services.The 2024/2025 forecast anticipates normal to above-normal rainfall, potentially influenced by La Niña. Rain could improve agricultural prospects, but increases risks of flooding and storm damage, particularly in river basins. The likelihood of frequent storms underscores the urgent need for climate resilience.The Government of Mozambique and partners have taken proactive steps, preparing a multi-sectoral drought appeal. This proposal highlights the urgency of adaptive actions to prevent deterioration and bolster resilience in Mozambique. Addressing immediate humanitarian needs while fostering climate adaptation will reduce vulnerability in the targeted affected communities.The Food Security Cluster plans to support 1.1 million people in IPC Phases 3 and 4 across 102 drought-affected districts giving priority to those in IPC4 and IPC3 and affected by Drought Severity Level 1. Thus, this project will support 225,500 people most vulnerable affected by the El Nino-induced drought in the provinces of Manica (districts of Guro, Macossa and Tambara) and Sofala (district of Maringue) with agricultural inputs for the main agricultural campaign to urgently restore their livelihoods.In line with this prioritization, the project will support 112,500 people with agricultural inputs for the main agricultural season and protected 144,000 cattle and chicken from 102,500 people against diseases. The project will also implement a climate component with actions aiming to contribute to building adaptive capacity and resilience of 10,500 with activities related to seed multiplication, promotion of climate-smart agricultural practices and vegetable production using water saving irrigation equipment and a collaboration with WFP where FAO will lead the training of beneficiaries on the production side, including the operation and maintenance of the systems while WFP will lead the post-harvest management component.The project objective, results and targets are as follows:Impact: Resilience of the targeted households is increased Project objective: Improve the food security of households affected by El Nino-induced drought in Manica and Sofala provinces Outcome 1 - Food security of households affected by El Nino-induced drought in Manica and Sofala provinces improvedOutput 1.1 – Crop production of 112,500 people most vulnerable restored Output 1.2 – 144,000 Poultry and cattle protected against diseases (from 102,500 people)Outcome 2 - Resilience of the communities to climate shocks increased (targeting 10,500 people)Output 2.1 – Climate-resilient agricultural practices promoted Output 2.2 – Beneficiaries' conscious of climate-smart and sustainable agriculture practices
